name: unixcw
desc: Morse code tutor and command-line tools
why: Morse code tutor and tools that turn your keyboard into a telegraph trainer, a classic old-school sound toy.

brief.what_it_is: unixcw is a project that provides the libcw library and a set of command-line programs built on it: cw, cwgen, cwcp, and xcwcp. The programs help people learn to send and receive Morse code. The homepage does not describe inputs and outputs in detail, so the exact interaction (keyboard, audio, text) is not confirmed from this page. Brew lists the executables as cw, cwcp, and cwgen.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the programs are intended for people who want to learn receiving and sending Morse code. The original developer was Simon Baldwin, and Kamil Ignacak took over maintenance in 2011.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a 'Get unixcw' link, but I did not follow it, so I have no install steps beyond what brew reports. The project is developed and tested on GNU/Linux.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, GPL-licensed Morse trainer that ships a library (libcw) alongside several front-ends, including an X11 version (xcwcp) in addition to the terminal tools.
brief.status: Maintained, with evidence from the homepage: current version 3.6.1, published November 2023, and a copyright line running to 2023. I did not see a commit history or a release page to confirm more recent activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the project is developed and tested on GNU/Linux only, so other platforms are unverified. I did not read the README, docs, or the SourceForge page, so install details, options, and the sound or keyboard behaviour are not confirmed. Brew's caveats field is empty. The scout note calls it a 'sound toy', but the homepage does not mention audio, so treat that as unverified.
